verses.zh: 此后，我听见好像群众在天上大声说：哈利路亚（就是要赞美耶和华的意思）！救恩、荣耀、权能都属乎我们的　神！
verses.en: After these things I heard what sounded like the loud voice of a vast throng in heaven, saying,“Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God,

verses.zh: 他的判断是真实公义的；因他判断了那用淫行败坏世界的大淫妇，并且向淫妇讨流仆人血的罪，给他们伸冤。
verses.en: because his judgments are true and just.[NOTE:1] For he has judged[NOTE:2] the great prostitutewho corrupted the earth with her sexual immorality,and has avenged the blood of his servants[NOTE:3] poured out by her own hands!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Compare the similar phrase in Rev 16:7.
Or “has punished.” See BDAG 568 s.v. κρίνω 5.b.α, describing the OT background which involves both the vindication of the innocent and the punishment of the guilty.
See the note on the word “servants” in 1:1.
Grk “from her hand” (referring to her responsibility in causing the blood of God’s followers to be shed).

verses.zh: 又说：哈利路亚！烧淫妇的烟往上冒，直到永永远远。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] a second time the crowd shouted, “Hallelujah!” The smoke rises from her forever and ever.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
Or “her smoke ascends forever and ever.”

verses.zh: 那二十四位长老与四活物就俯伏敬拜坐宝座的　神，说：阿们！哈利路亚！
verses.en: The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures threw themselves to the ground[NOTE:1] and worshiped God, who was seated on the throne, saying: “Amen! Hallelujah!”
notes: Grk “creatures fell down.” BDAG 815 s.v. πίπτω 1.b.α.ב. has “fall down, throw oneself to the ground as a sign of devotion or humility, before high-ranking persons or divine beings.”

verses.zh: 有声音从宝座出来说：　神的众仆人哪，凡敬畏他的，无论大小，都要赞美我们的　神！
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] a voice came from the throne, saying: “Praise our Godall you his servants,and all you who fear him,both the small and the great!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.

verses.zh: 我听见好像群众的声音，众水的声音，大雷的声音，说：哈利路亚！因为主―我们的　神、全能者作王了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I heard what sounded like the voice of a vast throng, like the roar of many waters and like loud crashes of thunder. They were shouting:[NOTE:2] “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God,[NOTE:3] the All-Powerful,[NOTE:4] reigns!
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
Grk “like the voice of a large crowd…saying.” Because of the complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation by supplying the words “They were.”

Several mss (א2 P 1611 2053 2344 MK lat) read “the Lord our God” (κύριος ὁ θεός ἡμῶν, kurios ho theos hēmōn). Other significant mss (A 1006 1841), however, omit the “our” (ἡμῶν). Further, certain mss (051 MA) omit “Lord” (κύριος), while others (including א*) change the order of the statement to “God our Lord” (ὁ θεός ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν). The expression “the Lord God, the All-Powerful” occurs in 6 other places in Revelation (1:8; 4:8; 11:17; 15:3; 16:7; 21:22) and the pronoun “our” is never used. Scribes familiar with the expression in this book, and especially with the frequent κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ (kurios ho theos ho pantokratōr; “the Lord God, the All-Powerful”) in the OT Prophets (LXX; cf. Jer 39:19; Hos 12:6; Amos 3:13; 4:13; 5:8, 14, 15, 16, 27; 9:5, 6, 15; Nah 3:5; Zech 10:3), would naturally omit the pronoun. Its presence may have arisen due to liturgical motivations or to conform to the expression “our God” in 19:1, 5, but this seems much less likely than an aversion to using the pronoun here and only here in the Greek Bible in the fuller title κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ.
On this word BDAG 755 s.v. παντοκράτωρ states, “the Almighty, All-Powerful, Omnipotent (One) only of God…(ὁ) κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ π.…Rv 1:8; 4:8; 11:17; 15:3; 16:7; 21:22…κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν ὁ π. Rv 19:6.”

verses.zh: 我们要欢喜快乐，将荣耀归给他。因为，羔羊婚娶的时候到了；新妇也自己预备好了，
verses.en: Let us rejoice[NOTE:1] and exultand give him glory,because the wedding celebration of the Lamb has come,and his bride has made herself ready.
notes: This verb and the next two verbs are hortatory subjunctives (giving exhortations).

verses.zh: 就蒙恩得穿光明洁白的细麻衣。（这细麻衣就是圣徒所行的义。）
verses.en: She was permitted to be dressed in bright, clean, fine linen”[NOTE:1] (for the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints).[NOTE:2]
notes: On the term translated “fine linen,” BDAG 185 s.v. βύσσινος states, “made of fine linen, subst. τὸ β. fine linen, linen garment…Rv 18:12…16; 19:8, 14.”
This phrase is treated as a parenthetical explanation by the author.

verses.zh: 天使吩咐我说：「你要写上：凡被请赴羔羊之婚筵的有福了！」又对我说：「这是　神真实的话。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the angel[NOTE:2] said to me, “Write the following: Blessed are those who are invited to the banquet at the wedding celebration of the Lamb!” He also said to me, “These are the true words of God.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (the angel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 我就俯伏在他脚前要拜他。他说：「千万不可！我和你，并你那些为耶稣作见证的弟兄同是作仆人的，你要敬拜　神。」因为预言中的灵意乃是为耶稣作见证。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] I threw myself down[NOTE:2] at his feet to worship him, but[NOTE:3] he said, “Do not do this![NOTE:4] I am only[NOTE:5] a fellow servant[NOTE:6] with you and your brothers and sisters[NOTE:7] who hold to the testimony about[NOTE:8] Jesus. Worship God, for the testimony about Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the angel’s announcement.
Grk “I fell down at his feet.” BDAG 815 s.v. πίπτω 1.b.α.ב. has “fall down, throw oneself to the ground as a sign of devotion or humility, before high-ranking persons or divine beings.”
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
On the elliptical expression ὅρα μή (hora mē) BDAG 720 s.v. ὁράω B.2 states: “Elliptically…ὅρα μή (sc. ποιήσῃς) watch out! don’t do that! Rv 19:10; 22:9.”
The lowliness of a slave is emphasized in the Greek text with the emphatic position of σύνδουλος (sundoulos). The use of “only” helps to bring this nuance out in English.
Grk “fellow slave.” See the note on the word “servants” in v. 2.
The Greek term “brother” literally refers to family relationships, but here it is used in a broader sense to connote familial relationships within the family of God (cf. BDAG 18 s.v. ἀδελφός 2.a).
The genitive ᾿Ιησοῦ (Iēsou) has been translated as an objective genitive here. A subjective genitive, also possible, would produce the meaning “who hold to what Jesus testifies.”

verses.zh: 我观看，见天开了。有一匹白马，骑在马上的称为诚信真实，他审判，争战，都按着公义。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I saw heaven opened and here came[NOTE:2] a white horse! The[NOTE:3] one riding it was called “Faithful” and “True,” and with justice[NOTE:4] he judges and goes to war.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
The phrase “and here came” expresses the sense of καὶ ἰδού (kai idou).
A new sentence was started in the translation at this point and καί (kai) was not translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “in righteousness,” but since the context here involves the punishment of the wicked and the vindication of the saints, “justice” was preferred.

verses.zh: 他的眼睛如火焰，他头上戴着许多冠冕；又有写着的名字，除了他自己没有人知道。
verses.en: His eyes are like a fiery[NOTE:1] flame and there are many diadem crowns[NOTE:2] on his head. He has[NOTE:3] a name written[NOTE:4] that no one knows except himself.
notes: The genitive noun πυρός (puros) has been translated as an attributive genitive (see also Rev 1:14).

For the translation of διάδημα (diadēma) as “diadem crown” see L&N 6.196.sn Diadem crowns were a type of crown used as a symbol of the highest ruling authority in a given area, and thus often associated with kingship.
Grk “head, having.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Although many translations supply a prepositional phrase to specify what the name was written on (“upon Him,” NASB; “on him,” NIV), there is no location for the name specified in the Greek text.

verses.zh: 他穿着溅了血的衣服；他的名称为　神之道。
verses.en: He is dressed in clothing dipped[NOTE:1] in blood, and he is called[NOTE:2] the Word of God.
notes: It appears that “dipped” (βεβαμμένον, bebammenon), supported by several majuscules and other witnesses (A 051 M), is the original reading. Due to the lack of the preposition “in” (ἐν, en) after the verb (βεβαμμένον αἵματι, bebammenon haimati), and also probably because of literary allusions to Isa 63:3, several mss and versions seem to have changed the text to “sprinkled” (either ῥεραντισμένον [rherantismenon] in P 2329 al; ἐρραντισμένον [errantismenon] in 1006 1841; ἐρραμμένον [errammenon] in 2053 2062; or ῥεραμμένον [rherammenon] in 1611; or in one case περιρεραμμένον [perirerammenon] in א[2]). The reading most likely to give rise to the others is “dipped.”tn Or perhaps “soaked.”
Grk “the name of him is called.”

verses.zh: 在天上的众军骑着白马，穿着细麻衣，又白又洁，跟随他。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] armies that are in heaven, dressed in white, clean, fine linen,[NOTE:2] were following him on white horses.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
On the term translated “fine linen,” BDAG 185 s.v. βύσσινος states, “made of fine linen, subst. τὸ β. fine linen, linen garment…Rv 18:12, 16; 19:8, 14.”

verses.zh: 有利剑从他口中出来，可以击杀列国。他必用铁杖辖管（辖管：原文是牧）他们，并要踹全能　神烈怒的酒榨。
verses.en: From his mouth extends a sharp sword so that with it he can strike the nations.[NOTE:1] He[NOTE:2] will rule[NOTE:3] them with an iron rod,[NOTE:4] and he stomps the winepress[NOTE:5] of the furious[NOTE:6] wrath of God, the All-Powerful.[NOTE:7]
notes: Or “the Gentiles” (the same Greek word may be translated “Gentiles” or “nations”).
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “will shepherd.”
Or “scepter.” The Greek term ῥάβδος (rhabdos) can mean either “rod” or “scepter.” sn A quotation from Ps 2:9 (see also Rev 2:27; 12:5).
He stomps the winepress. See Isa 63:3, where Messiah does this alone (usually several individuals would join in the process), and Rev 14:20.

The genitive θυμοῦ (thumou) has been translated as an attributed genitive. Following BDAG 461 s.v. θυμός 2, the combination of the genitives of θυμός (thumos) and ὀργή (orgē) in Rev 16:19 and 19:15 are taken to be a strengthening of the thought as in the OT and Qumran literature (Exod 32:12; Jer 32:37; Lam 2:3; CD 10:9).
On this word BDAG 755 s.v. παντοκράτωρ states, “the Almighty, All-Powerful, Omnipotent (One) only of God…(ὁ) κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ π.…Rv 1:8; 4:8; 11:17; 15:3; 16:7; 21:22.”

verses.zh: 在他衣服和大腿上有名写着说：「万王之王，万主之主。」
verses.en: He has a name written on his clothing and on his thigh: “King of kings and Lord of lords.”

verses.zh: 我又看见一位天使站在日头中，向天空所飞的鸟大声喊着说：「你们聚集来赴　神的大筵席，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I saw one angel standing in[NOTE:2] the sun, and he shouted in a loud voice to all the birds flying high in the sky:[NOTE:3] “Come, gather around for the great banquet[NOTE:4] of God,
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
The precise significance of ἐν (en) here is difficult to determine.

On μεσουρανήματι (mesouranēmati) here see L&N 1.10: “high in the sky, midpoint in the sky, directly overhead, straight above in the sky.” The birds mentioned here are carrion birds like vultures, circling high overhead, and now being summoned to feast on the corpses.
This is the same Greek word (δεῖπνον, deipnon) used in 19:9.

verses.zh: 可以吃君王与将军的肉，壮士与马和骑马者的肉，并一切自主的为奴的，以及大小人民的肉。」
verses.en: to eat[NOTE:1] your fill[NOTE:2] of the flesh of kings, the flesh of generals,[NOTE:3] the flesh of powerful people, the flesh of horses and those who ride them, and the flesh of all people, both free and slave,[NOTE:4] and small and great!”
notes: The ἵνα (hina) clause, insofar as it is related to the first imperative, has the force of an imperative.
The idea of eating “your fill” is evident in the context with the use of χορτάζω (chortazō) in v. 21.
Grk “chiliarchs”; normally a chiliarch was a military officer commanding a thousand soldiers, but here probably used of higher-ranking commanders like generals (see L&N 55.15; cf. Rev 6:15).
See the note on the word “servants” in 1:1.

verses.zh: 我看见那兽和地上的君王，并他们的众军都聚集，要与骑白马的并他的军兵争战。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies assembled to do battle with the one who rode the horse and with his army.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.

verses.zh: 那兽被擒拿；那在兽面前曾行奇事、迷惑受兽印记和拜兽像之人的假先知，也与兽同被擒拿。他们两个就活活地被扔在烧着硫磺的火湖里；
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] the beast was seized, and along with him the false prophet who had performed the signs on his behalf[NOTE:2]—signs by which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped his image. Both of them were thrown alive into the lake of fire burning with sulfur.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the introduction of an unexpected development in the account: The opposing armies do not come together in battle; rather the leader of one side is captured.
For this meaning see BDAG 342 s.v. ἐνώπιον 4.b, “by the authority of, on behalf of Rv 13:12, 14; 19:20.”
Traditionally, “brimstone.”

verses.zh: 其余的被骑白马者口中出来的剑杀了；飞鸟都吃饱了他们的肉。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] others were killed by the sword that extended from the mouth of the one who rode the horse, and all the birds gorged[NOTE:2] themselves with their flesh.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

On the translation of ἐχορτάσθησαν (echortasthēsan) BDAG 1087 s.v. χορτάζω 1.a states, “of animals, pass. in act. sense πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα ἐχορτάσθησαν ἐκ τῶν σαρκῶν αὐτῶν all the birds gorged themselves with their flesh Rv 19:21 (cp. TestJud. 21:8).”
